running_head.number_position: inside the text column: flush with the column's right edge (the right end of the head rule and of the body lines), separated from the italic title by space

printed.above_head: a small vertical mark at the top right; specks between title and number

section_headings.as_printed: II. Legists¹. (capitals and small capitals, superscript footnote reference 1 before the full stop)
section_headings.look: centred, roman capitals and small capitals, same style as 'I. The Medieval Publicists.', large space above and below; the E is damaged in the scan (reads like 'LEGISTS' with a broken E)

entries.setting: Each entry has a hanging number in bold sans-serif figures with a full stop (e.g. '8.'), set flush with the left edge of the column; the entry text is roman (author name in the same plain roman as the rest, not small caps or italic), first line beside the number, turnover lines indented further (hanging indent).

margin_numbers.side: left, hanging (inside the column's left edge, the entry numbers)

foot.footnote: ¹ On pp. 186, 238, 351 and 416 Dr Gierke gives long lists of legists and canonists. We here select only such writers as are referred to in the chapter that is here translated.

printed.notes: Section heading sits below a blank band under the head rule. The footnote reference is on the section heading.
